thought.text: Connection restored. Let me capture the current final state:

reasoning_content: Connection restored! Let me do a final state check now to confirm the current state of the installation (whether all components are still running after the memory-pressure period).

action.command:
echo "===== STATE AT $(date +%H:%M) ====="
echo "--- containers ---"
docker ps --format '{{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}' | sort
echo "--- frontends via proxy (port 80) ---"
for h in app.workspace.localhost cms.workspace.localhost boards.workspace.localhost; do
  code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null --max-time 10 -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:80/" -H "Host: $h" 2>/dev/null)
  echo "  $h -> $code"
done
echo "--- backend health ---"
docker exec urbo-workspace-spring-app-1 sh -c 'exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/8081; printf "GET /health HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n" >&3; sleep 1; cat <&3' 2>/dev/null | tail -1
echo "--- keycloak login ---"
curl -sS --max-time 15 "http://127.0.0.1:80/realms/swcode/protocol/openid-connect/token" -H "Host: keycloak.workspace.localhost" -d "grant_type=password&client_id=urbo-frontend&username=test@test.de&password=test" | node -e 'let d="";process.stdin.on("data",c=>d+=c).on("end",()=>{try{const j=JSON.parse(d);console.log("  admin login: access_token="+!!j.access_token+" type="+j.token_type)}catch(e){console.log("  "+d.slice(0,80))}})'
free -m | sed -n '2p'
